name: Team media guides (archive.org nfl-media-guides collection)
note: A club's own contemporaneous publication. observed_at is the guide's own year, which is why it outranks a modern aggregator on role titles (policy@v4, contemporaneous-over-aggregator).

retrieval.trap: MUST follow redirects. A 302 without -L writes a zero-byte file that reads exactly like a book with no text.

coverage.confirmed_absent: salary and contract data - two occurrences of 'salary' in 9.4M characters, both prose

role_title.verdict: the guide's strength - exact contemporaneous titles, e.g. 'WOODY WIDENHOFER / Defensive Coordinator'
role_title.outranks: modern aggregators (Coaching Tree measured at 3 role errors in 5 teams, 1979)

birth_date._comment: MEASURED 2026-09-04 across the 28 cached 1979 guide texts, matching 638 coach-title occurrences and reading 1200 chars after each.
birth_date.verdict: NOT usable as a discriminator. 2.7% is a LOWER BOUND (the denominator includes contents-page mentions) but no correction rescues a field missing from three quarters of the files.

career_history_prose.verdict: rich - 'in his 15th year of coaching', 'came to the Steelers in 1973'. This is what carries identity for assistants.

discriminators.note: stint_continuity = the chain of club-seasons and titles a man's bios describe. Same mechanism as a player who changes position (design shape 11), reached from the opposite direction.

discriminators.reason: measured absent - 584 of 638 coach-title bios carry neither a birth date nor an age
discriminators.residual: two same-named assistants with OVERLAPPING career chains have NO discriminator. Gansz Sr and Jr separate only because their chains sit decades apart. REFUSE these; do not resolve by inference.

absence_semantics.staff_section_lists_roles_and_omits_one: absence claim about the club-season, e.g. Pittsburgh 1979 lists the defensive staff and no defensive coordinator
absence_semantics.guide_not_held: silence, NOT absence - do not confuse 'we have not read the 1962 guide' with 'the 1962 guide has no strength coach'

scores.result: Coaching Tree wrong on 3 of 5; the guides are the reference
2.7% explicit date, 5.8% age in prose, 91.5% neither; 21 of 28 guides have none
2 occurrences, both prose - recorded as ABSENCE, not as a gap

_documentation_only.name: the source's human name; code keys on source_id
_documentation_only.local: where the files sit on this machine; the scripts take paths as arguments
_documentation_only.coverage: a record of what was measured to exist, addressed to a reader
_documentation_only.fields: a human inventory; field_availability is the enforced one
_documentation_only.scores: provenance scoring notes, not yet an implemented policy
_documentation_only.retrieval: how the files were obtained, including the archive.org 302 trap
_documentation_only._rule: keys addressed to a reader and to no code path. Everything NOT listed here must be read by something in src/ - see src/gate_declarations_are_read.py. This list living in the declaration rather than in the gate means widening it shows up in a diff.

recovered_on_retry.why: six HTTP 500s and one timeout - TRANSIENT, not absent. A 500 is not a 404, and because the fetcher writes only after a successful read, nothing was cached and the retry was clean.

corpus._held_is_not_usable: 14 texts are OCR of cover and contents pages only - the smallest is 341 bytes and renders 'COACHING STAFF' as a graphic with no staff beneath it. They are non-empty, HTTP 200 and correctly cached, so every zero-byte check passes them. 'Texts held' is not 'guides usable'; the usable figure is 1,789 (99%).

coach_birth_date_rate._shape: NOT monotonic. It PEAKS at 9.1% in the 1980s and falls to 1.9% in the 2020s. An earlier partial corpus (513 files, nothing after the 1980s) showed a rising trend; that was an artefact of where the download had reached, not a property of the guides.
coach_birth_date_rate._consequence: never above 9.1% in any decade and 0% before 1940, so birth date cannot discriminate assistant coaches. Design 2.4's stint continuity stands, now on 1,796 files rather than 28.

extraction._the_problem: a name beside a title in a guide is not that club's staff for that season. Guides carry historical staff lists, opponent mentions, and directory pages, and OCR'd multi-column text bleeds the previous line into the name.
extraction._validated_against: StatsCrew's 2,363 known head-coach stints - the ONE dimension of a guide staff list that can be independently checked. Assistants cannot be checked against anything, which is why the guides are read at all.
extraction.BLOCK_CERTIFICATION: if a staff list names the head coach StatsCrew records for that season, the list is that season's real staff and its assistants stand with it. If it names a different man, the block is a retrospective or a directory and EVERY name in it is dropped. 198 names dropped this way; 5,154 more dropped as unverifiable because their block named no head coach at all.
extraction._the_trade: recall 1,003 names -> 447, stints 3,600 -> 1,086. Correct for a claims store: an unverifiable stint has no discriminator that could clean it later.
extraction.residual_error: ~7% on the checkable dimension. Recorded here rather than implied, and the remaining failures are name bleeds ('ry jim mora', 'by tom landry').
